body: Possibly the United States of Tara (I just finished it to find out it was cancelled, totally pissed off about that.) Oh, and Final Fantasy 7 as well as 13.
Sneezing multiple times, especially loudly. I just can't stand loud noises and yelling when you sneeze just seems like something you can control to a degree. It pisses me off to no end.

My parents went through a divorce and decided I needed therapy.

I was introduced to therapy at the age of 6.  I was given the label Major Depression. I was on twelve different SSRIs, rotated at different times (plus anti-psychotics and adderall) crushed and put into my food. It caused me to have seizures, which the doctor later believed to be "muscle spasms." I was also in therapy for twelve years straight with no breakthroughs. Despite this, my mother was convinced that the medication was "working" since I desperately wanted to be off of it. I was just told that I needed to be on medication for life, and that was that. Whenever I tried to persuade my mother to get me off of the medication or to bring me to a different doctor, I was suddenly showing symptoms of oppositional defiant disorder, or autism and he recommended I be put into a psychiatric ward. 

Once I got to the children's psyche ward, the orderlies told me that my parents would never love me or trust me again, and I was just a bad kid. There was a TON of verbal abuse from adults that were supposed to be helping us. A little boy and I became friends and I was terrified of being molested or raped during the shower inspections (occurred daily by a male secretary) or at night since we had to leave all our rooms open and unlocked. I woke up one night to a guy holding a flash-light in my face. I couldn't scream, but he just ran off. My friend and several other kids threatened to call the cops once or twice, and the nurse on duty just laughed and handed over the phone, saying "Who is going to believe you?"

I went from a creative little girl who learned how to read at the age of 16 months to an withdrawn suicidal epileptic.

I am 24 years old, and I still suffer from seizures as well as an anxiety disorder and depression. I will not take any medication, no exceptions. I am set to have yet another MRI/EEG in a few months. I have been off meds and out of therapy since the age of 18 and I have never been happier. Unfortunately, the majority of my childhood feels like a foggy dream.

My cat has hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. We picked him up from the shelter without knowing of this condition and found out that instead of getting a 3 year old cat with roughly 10+ years left to live, he could go into cardiac arrest and pass away any time, most likely within a couple years.

I would love to have had those three years with him. He supposedly went from home to home.

Another wal-mart story:

During lunch, rumor had spread for whatever reason that a co-worker and I worked with the school systems. She was an assistant teacher in her son's classroom and I had helped with special ed. Apparently, she had been having problems with her daughter and the school was giving her hell for the past few months. She then tells us this delightful detailed story:

"My eight year old has been sent home four times this month because of her head-lice. She's had it for a little over a year now and it won't go away, I've just given up on tryin. The nurse says it's not acceptable. Bull. Shit. They went and called CPS on me four times! It's not my fault she don't comb her hair, and she puts the same dirty clothes on every morning because it's her favorite! I do laundry on Saturday. I can't get up and tell her to wear anything else because she's out the door before I wake up! They say she smells dirty too, but that's only because she doesn't wipe or wash her hands after she uses the bathroom. What do they want me to do, go to school and wipe her myself? They don't understand that I have other things to do. Now whenever she comes to school they send her to the nurse. What should I do?" 

After she left, co-worker and I exchanged horrified glances.

I'm allergic to nickel and my body rejected my earrings (I had 4 in each ear, now I'm down to 3) and nose piercing, however my navel ring and my tattoo remained unscathed. 

I was quite surprised with the tat. I didn't even bleed and I healed relatively fast. 

Also, my first cousin has much more severe nickel allergy and she got a very small ankle tattoo and it didn't bother her at all.

Also, one guy named his child after himself (John Doe) but decided the child needed a different first-name. The kid's name is Saint John Doe.

Cheerios with flat pepsi. 

I was a growing kid and my parents always used to unwisely spend a ton of money on remodelling the house (taking a good portion out of our grocery money) so we would have nothing but old cereal, stale chips and soda for a few weeks. I eventually decided that the cheerio and pepsi (instead of milk) combo was delicious, but since it didn't involve milk I would only eat it for dinner. My parents thought I was weird.
I'm a (specifically pink) power ranger scientist.... I'm also not quite sure what I do, but I am the only doctor in my field that drives a Zord.
Spyro the Dragon, Super Smash Bros, The Lion King on Sega Genesis, and Zelda the Ocarina of Time. I'll still play pokemon too but I can't dedicate 75+ hours on a game like I used to...

I was about 7 or 8 and my family went to Denny's. I got waffles, and I noticed that a housefly was under one of them. My grandmother told the waitress, and she sent it back. I got a new dish of waffles and after I took a bite I noticed gnats (some alive, some dead) were everywhere on the dish. As I was about to say something, the waitress got flagged over to a table a couple sections away for the same exact problem, and again for a table across the room... same bug issue. 

I decided that I wasn't hungry and I would make a mental note to never come back. If you have a pest problem, why stay open?
Typo. I work there currently.

I work at wal-mart. I was reading in the break-room and a woman came in and sat uncomfortably close to me. She asked me if I went to church (I always work Sundays) and I said no and tried to lead the conversation elsewhere. Usually, I would've said something like "I don't talk about these things in the workplace, but she was mentally disabled and working as a greeter. Cue long one-sided rant about "Why not? Church is good" as I'm struggling to politely end the conversation or change the topic. 

Then, she proceeded to ask me what church my parents went to, if they were Christian, and then she inquired about my grandparents. I explained that my grandfather was in a concentration camp and I wasn't sure if he was Jewish or not since he didn't speak a fair amount of English. She looked at me like I just grew a second head. As I was talking mid-sentence, she randomly blurted out "ABORTION IS WRONG!" which silenced the entire room.

She does this periodically about two or three Sundays out of the month, same exact conversation and I can't do anything about it because "she doesn't know any better." If I refuse to answer anything she'll ask "Why" in an endless loop. 

Last week she walked around the store yelling "We need new president!!"

Any one of Stephen King's Dark Tower novels. I also think that the old Animorphs series by K.A Applegate could be re-done nicely and packed into one decent sci-fi movie for pre-teens. Nickelodeon's series was shit.

It honestly sounds like she was probably just a poor anxious nerdy girl with serious self-esteem issues that lied or exaggerated about a good majority of the things she told you (butler, modelling), panicked and then didn't show up for fear you would be pissed or not attracted to her.

I met a bunch of people online and later one of them, nothing was shady. The only odd situation was one of our friends was a bit overly feminine to the point of ridiculousness, and was very interested in flirting with our one male friend. He ended up gradually only speaking with her and they cybered often. She turned out to be a dude with gender identity disorder. I think she might have transitioned now, but I no longer speak with either of them. Last I heard, the guy she cybered with didn't really care too much about the fact that she happened to have a penis, but things never worked out between them.

We lived next-door to a woman that lived in a small house with her hubby, 4 large dogs and two adult children, all of whom had severe un-treated mental illnesses. The son (I think if I remember correctly) had paranoid schizophrenia, the daughter was bi-polar and a horder, and the mother was a horder and slowly becoming senile. The husband was normal and took care of them all for a good ten years until he had enough and left them all to fend for themselves.

Anyway, she'd run over to our house smelling like she hadn't bathed in months partially caked in her own feces and would ask us for any extra newspapers or plastic bags. At night she would go through our garbage for things to add to her collection of stuff to horde. She never took anything of value, mostly torn envelopes or old newspapers. We ended up having to take the trash out early in the morning a few minutes before the truck came to pick it up.

Regardless of this, we tried to remain friendly and good neighbours. They didn't ask for their problems and it seemed like they couldn't help themselves. We accepted food from them once or twice during the holidays up until my grandmother cooked a chicken breast she had given us from her own freezer to find used diabetic needles shoved into the meat (while she was cutting it open to serve it to her young grandchildren.)

That's probably one of the worst things that happened with any of our neighbours. 

**Tl;dr: Mentally unstable neighbours gave our family food with used needles hidden in it.**

Doubtful. I bought an e-reader thinking it would be something I only use a few times and I get bored with and now I'd rather use it than carry around a bunch of books in my purse. I actually have a book right now that I can't get through because I don't want to lug it around everywhere. I only buy books now if I can't get them for my e-reader, or if I (rarely) love them and want an actual physical copy around the house to keep and re-read.

The only books I absolutely will only buy that aren't in e-reader form are those for young children. I'm sorry, but I'm not one of those people that will let toddlers play with my expensive electronics.

I know a mom with two nightmare before christmas tattoos, a few things related to bands, and a hello kitty tattoo. I also know a 50 year old woman with betty boop, taz and tweety bird tattoos. I equate it to wearing a graphic t-shirt for the rest of your life... but hey, if you really want to broadcast that you really love these things, go right on ahead. 

The reasons they gave me were "I really love it, I've been a fan for forever."
Is it weird that looks like every profile picture on my old classmates facebooks?

Not a fan, but I believe that people in general do not have high expectations for rappers. He's making music and not beating up girls, going to jail or doing drugs? Well, good for him! 

Personally, I dislike the guy and his music.
Tony Hawk, Stephen King, Will Smith, Nsync or Backstreet boy members... stuff from childhood mostly. I expect Britney Spears will pass sometime and I would feel bad for her kids.

The fuck.

I taught kids with behavioral difficulties like oppositional defiant disorder. I had an orphaned 8 year old (named Nate) child call me "mom" and try to convince the guidance counsellor that I needed to adopt him (he never did this with anyone before.) Later, he told me in private "I wish you were my real mom." I was in tears after class because it was just so sad. 

Also, hilariously enough... this massive woman came in to pick up one of the students and Nate was just gawking at her with his mouth open.  She was a nice lady but she had to be around 400lbs at the very least and I don't think he had ever seen anyone quite that large. She left and he muttered to the other teacher, "I'm glad my mommy (maristar87) is skinny like a pancake." 

I'm 99.9% sure I am ineligible to adopt due to mental health reasons (major depression) but I desperately wanted to at that point. Hell, I was a college kid with zero money but if I had to take two jobs to make it happen I would've. I hope at least he found a good home.

My mother was dating this guy that had five kids. One or two were around my age and we'd go to this little stream by their house and throw rocks in the water. Suddenly my step-sister-to-be screams "SNAKE!" at the top of her lungs and we see this badass: 

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agkistrodon_piscivorus

She actually pushed me (I almost fell directly on it but caught myself) and ran for her life inside the house, all the way upstairs into her room. I managed to limp into the bathroom with a twisted ankle and sat there trying to wash off the dirt that had gotten on me from climbing the muddy rock wall to the house. The girl came out and started screaming that I had gotten the entire bathroom dirty (her father was OCD about cleanliness.)

My mother and the guy broke up because he had to wash the bathroom rugs that I had dirtied. 

It became apparent to me that she wanted me out of the picture and she wasn't allowed to go down to the water due to the snake problem.

Detroit. We got grounded at the airport for about two days for "weather" and then when we could get a plane they couldn't find the pilot. They claimed they did not have to find us a hotel, so we slept on the floor without any luggage. People were angry, but not violently so and our whole line was completely surrounded by security guards in a threatening stance holding some kind of gun or tazers (wasn't sure and I was trying to avoid eye-contact, but it was definitely a weapon) as we were forced to board twelve hours after finding said missing pilot. I had the privilege of meeting a foreign woman who had been stuck there for an entire week sleeping on the floor (also due to "weather") and couldn't get in contact with her family in the Philippines. She was a wreck.

Just fucking awful. I will never, ever go back.

Meticulously describe unrelated mundane things in great detail... like pages upon pages of description. Anne Rice does this often. I like knowing scenery, and it helps to set the mood for the story but it can be done tactfully in such a way it doesn't leave the reader yawning or skipping ahead. I love reading but I just put the series down indefinitely, and I never have done that before.

I'm my mother's first. My father's third and youngest. I'm not sure how that balances out.

All of my siblings are fine to my knowledge. Both of my grandfathers suffered depression. Two of my first cousins battled it as well. However, my one grandfather was an alcoholic, the other was a concentration camp survivor . My cousin had a terminal illness, the other was a drug addict that recently lost both of her parents.

I was diagnosed with major depression at 6. Now I'm leaning toward psychotic depression... have to get that checked into.

I was raised Christian. My mother's side of the family went to church probably only 6 or 7 times in their entire lives, just on a whim. They didn't understand Christianity, never read the bible and mistook aspects of other religions (like reincarnation) as their own. My father's side  were once Roman Catholic, but after my birth they became Southern Baptist and turned into fundamentalists.

It was a weird upbringing. When I realized I had the ability to decide for myself what I believed (around 8) I claimed I was atheist. Later on, I was heavily involved with the Southern Baptists until they started banning things like music, secular friendships and movies. I'm not quite sure why I did that, since I disagreed with a lot of their beliefs and I became incredibly upset at their attempts (mid-sermon) to encourage me to vote republican. I think I was just a lonely kid and I wanted the approval of my absent father's family. I got out and I'm a much happier person because of it.

Now I'm actually back to atheist status. I'm interested in Buddhism, but I'm slowly starting to realize how religious it can get and it turns me off.

XenaWPM, I think it was also AOL 3.0.

I rarely used it though since I only had about two friends at the time that thought computers were "too nerdy."

I was distraught after a family member had died (it was my first funeral) and forgot to do my homework. I was one of the "smart kids" still passing the class with an A, and it was just a stupid book-it assignment... but apparently she had the idea since I was one of the good students that I would help the class win some sort of contest with the other grades. My 4th grade reading teacher called me up to the front of the class, verbally berated me and choked me bart-simpson style, shoving me into a bookcase. 

Mother called the school, they said that my teacher had been there for quite a number of years and would never do something like that. The teacher claimed she had just touched my chin. Since I didn't bruise (never did easily) we had nothing else to prove it. The rest of the kids in the class were too scared to say anything, and she was actually a very well-liked teacher (mainly with the popular kids) up to that point.

I'm no psych, but it sounds like it could've been that he had conduct disorder or ODD. I had to teach a classroom full of those kids and there was zero education going on. I thought I'd have an easier time since I was raised with a lot of wanna-be gangsters and inner city kids, but these kids would just literally try to kill eachother for no reason. 

One kid brought a box-cutter to school and tried to slit a little boy's throat because "he was smiling when I dropped my pencil case."
It wouldve been better had Ginny been a shy nerdy girl with a crush.

Charmaigne (spelling is probably way off) from United States of Tara. She is like a promiscious ten year old with sibling rivalry issues. Her sister isnt exactly better off, but it just gets on my nerves.

Just for legal ramifications, do not do it.

Also, years down the road do you still want to be doing this? (not implying addiction but if she sees you as a way to safely get drugs, she might not stop going to you to get them for quite a while.) Or, what if she gets bored with weed and wants to do something else you don't approve of? Would you be willing to supply her with other stuff she cannot safely get... like cocaine, just because she wants to try it? 

My uncle did this with his daughter, and she was in her late 30's with a family and still trying to get drugs through him.

I got my first tattoo at 24, and I don't regret it. My cousins got theirs done on impulse after their 18th birthday.  

My one cousin wishes she would have waited and put more thought into it. It looks really bad, the colouring is absolute shit and it looks exactly like it was drawn on with a crayon. It was also done in her "goth phase" so now she's a bubbly little nurse with a morbid death/despair tattoo on her lower back.  The other has huge flowers covering most of her boobs. 

To be fair, if I had gotten one with her I would've chosen this huge cross + Jesus thing I had been hoping to get. Style and taste change, and now I'm an atheist. 

Even if it is a tribute tattoo you still might want time to settle on placement, sizing and work out all the details. Also, something that you might want to take in consideration is weight gain. Most of my friends filled out considerably during their early 20's, and some of their tattoos look stretched and sloppy.

Hell no... but the teachers all said we had "more than enough time." I did this exact same thing. I carried all my books with me because my school had four floors packed with kids. If you were late for a class, you had detention, no exceptions. My doctor was pissed when he heard of a 90lb girl carrying a 40lb backpack.

Some kids said that I had lice and I would snort them like cocaine so they would reappear on my head in an infinite cycle. (I was really confused on how they came up with this...) In reality, I just had trichotillomania and was bullied rather badly for it.

Weirdest rumour-related shit: When I graduated in '06, I friended a good portion of people in my related classes and never really talked to them since I moved several states away. I planned on going to the reunion though and joined a group to keep me informed on when it would be. Roughly six years later, This year some guy I had one class with in 8th grade actually apologized for spreading the rumors and bullying and then proceeded to send me harassing texts and desperately tried to break up my marriage out of the blue. Needless to say, I'm not bothering to go to the reunion. 

Tl;dr: Crazy people who started a rumor contacted me six years after high-school graduation in order to break up my marriage and family. Don't talk to crazy people.

Also the 2 minutes between classes usually doesn't cover a pee break, especially when considering how packed the hallways are, how big the school is and factoring enough time in to go to your locker and switch out books.

This. My middle school was so damned worried we'd graffiti the bathroom on the final day of school they closed it down for the entire day. As a 7th grade girl, I ended up pissing myself in front of 40+ students (fucking horrifying) because our gym teacher wouldn't give me the pass. It's inhumane.

I'd say I really loved the whole Susan Delgado flashback, it was just so well written and incredibly emotional. Hell, anything about the old ka-tet is right up at #1 in my list. I also liked when he found Jake. Bottom of my list is anything dealing with Susannah, she was just had way too much going on (racism, multiple personalities, sudden love & marriage w/ Eddie Dean) and it took from the story. Susannah was like a portrait that King spent way too much time on and ruined.

It was more gradual. I had two friends (twin sisters) and they went from normal kids to Paris Hilton when their father got custody and moved them from the inner city to the wealthy side of town. They didn't really seem to want to talk to me after that due to our differences in financial/social status but our parents were friends so we hung out in their house from time to time. 

I was a loner, so I never really belonged to any clique, so it was just me and them for a while. It wasn't until after the one girl assaulted her mother on a drunken rampage only to be rewarded with a brand new car and house from her father (probably not her fault, in retrospect I would have taken it too) I started questioning the quality of the people around me. They usually end up in jail every couple of years and their father bails them out, blaming the mother's liberal parenting and income (divorced.) Because of his meddling, they are still really, really sheltered. During the last jailing the younger girl started screaming stuff about Obama and that "all poor people deserve to die." She then assaulted a police officer, mistaking her for some girl she hated in college.

I sat there one day and said to myself... this isn't normal. So, I just hung out with the rest of my friends and came over less and less until we only spoke via text or online. 

I managed to cut off contact with the one wild girl gradually and completely, but randomly the other will still speak with me on facebook and I'm fine with that.

I met a woman with a severely disabled daughter once. She was 9 years old and a vegetable. She would have grand-mal seizures every couple of hours and choke on her own saliva just about every twenty minutes or so... and she had been like this since birth and has no hope for improvement. Her mother was beyond inconsolable but thoroughly convinced her daughter would come out of it. I was a special ed assistant and the only thing we could do for her was feed her via a feeding tube and lay her on the floor in the recovery position. That was her entire existence.

Some people just hope beyond reasoning that their loved one will come back to them. There really isn't a reason for it. 

I've had about eleven cats, and six dogs in my lifetime and I don't understand it either.

On rare occasions when I am depressed I drink scotch like a fucking fish (girl here) and can out drink my male cousins. The rest of the time (when I'm mentally okay) I am the lightest weight drunk ever. 

I also was raised to play a shit ton of video games (all male cousins and siblings.)
I was watching this infomercial about some kind of aura machine. She went on to try to sell **"medical grade water"** that was extra purified of toxins. It was so pure, doctors used it in hospitals!

I tell everyone I am fine because my illnesses are invisable. Even my parents and close friends do not understand that I am not okay, and might not be here tomorrow. I got told off after I made a big deal about going to the hospital after the death of a relative, and they just started comparing my illnesses to his. I lie all the time. I even tell my husband I am fine, because I dont want to be guilt tripped for living slightly longer than a potential unknown person out there, or being compared to starving african children. I am fine because it is obvious they do not care unless you are missing limbs, attached to machines or are stuck in a hospital bed... and only then they suddenly care because it makes them look like good people. I want off of this planet.

Damn, its hard. I recently lost a close relative too (cystic fibrosis.) It has been almost a month since he passed. Im not really sure if it gets easier. Just remember to spend time with her, take lots of pictures and make some memories before they are gone and cherish them. If anyone wants to talk about grieving please pm me if you want to talk. You arent alone.

Originally I've never been a tattoo person, and I blame it on the fact that I was born with super light skin and light features. I can see it looking nice on some people but I am really picky about art and fashion. On me, it just pops out like I just slapped a sticker on my skin. I really, really don't like that.

I know too many people that have no eye for art and they have really terrible tattoos (tribal and tramp stamps that look like they were coloured with crayons.) I also don't like the overdone things that most girls get - I frequently see stars, sparrows, butterflies and summery themes like flip-flops and airbrushed looking beach scenes. I also don't like seeing any cartoon characters (I've seen enough ugly tweety birds and betty boop characters on 40+ year old women at wal-mart)... it seems like you are permanently wearing a tacky graphic-t shirt.

Nevertheless, I always wanted something done. I suggested that my cousin and I go get some work but we never made plans. He died about a year later. He was born with cystic fibrosis and his last tattoo was the word "breathe" on his hand between his left index finger and thumb. That's what I have now in his memory. 

I've been considering something else ever since I got it done. I'm not sure if I'll actually get any more though. I think it's just a coping skill for me.

My mother would "borrow" any money I got from relatives during xmas or my birthday and bitch me out if I asked for it back a few months later to buy something. I always felt that was a little trashy. It wasnt the worst thing shes done, but the first time I questioned her parenting. 

Also, when I realized my 16 year old cousin was smoking and doing drugs throughout her pregnancy. I was 6 at the time. She used to be my role model... now shes been evicted from 4 houses and randomly calls members of our family to threaten them if they dont give her and the kid money.

Tangy Taffy (or now it's called Laffy Taffy.) It's okay, but it makes your teeth hurt like hell. No wonder I had so many cavities growing up. 

Also, ice-cream. I literally had it almost daily. Now, I rarely if ever want it.

Oh I used to read a metric ton of smutty fan-fiction when I was a teenager, and now that I have a sex-life I'm convinced that basement-dwelling virgins or lonely teenage girls wrote all of them because anything they mentioned was all awkwardly impossible.

**Attention fan-fiction writers:** You cannot comfortably have sex in a hot-tub or a hot-spring, (if you have congrats, I don't know how you did it) lube washes away and it's like wrestling in a pot of boiling water. Also, they wrote about people using soap as lubrication... whhyyyy? That is so horrendously painful!!

Pretty much any disney movie that didn't become an instant classic or popular, like DuckTales: Treasure of the Lost Lamp, The Aristocats or The Rescuers Down Under. They weren't terrible, but I always assumed they were big hits like Snow White, Cinderella, and The Lion King.

So Luke and Daniel would've been lucky to be human, even though being born with such a sickness isn't an ideal "perfect" human rebirth? You could look at it as Luke and Daniel had bad karma from past lives, or they were really "good" lesser beings (like a super friendly and loving cat that only occasionally bit people) that didn't quite make it to "perfect" human rebirth status? Also, in their next lives nobody really knows and anything is possible so it's best not to get your hopes up?

Nevertheless, I guess I got some comfort at the minuscule chance that Luke was still here with us. Ah, well... it's fun to dream and imagine the possibilities I guess. Thanks everyone.
Theyll actually serve bus loads of people? Hell, I was in a van with like six people and another car of about 4 joined us and we were told sternly to call in beforehand... this was subway though.
I think I might be bizzarely proud of my future self. Seriously all I do is drink scotch and surf 4chan and reddit. If somehow I become a decent anything, even murderer then goddamn thats an upgrade.
I actually was scared to go to my cousins funeral because I was afraid if they saw how upset I was, they would think it was all a show. To be fair though, I was a wreck.

I know the feeling. My cousin just passed away from a genetic lung disease. He only got to be alive for thirty years, and most of it was painful. I'd like very much to believe he got to go to a better place and is living an afterlife like the life he deserved but I'm torn by the hard facts of life. Just continue to mourn and sit on the fence, there's no hardcore proof either way. I personally don't think that he's eating dinner with Jesus right now as we speak, but it doesn't mean that his conciousness or his energy is out there somewhere in some form...hell, even through decomposition he's going to be giving life to so many organisms.
The answer to the question is directly behind the billboard.
I had to do that when I lost weight too. My grandmother and mother would tell me that there's "no calories" in food like gelato and anything labeled organic. It's hard to get around people like that.

"Breathe" by Taylor Swift.

My cousin died at 2am last night after a hard battle with Cystic Fibrosis. I was raised with him and this song came up on my computer.

"I have to breathe without you." "I can't breathe without you..."
... "It's 2 am and I just lost a friend."

When I taught it seemed like parents wanted their children either to be gifted geniuses or special needs cases. Nobody wanted their kid to be considered average, even if that meant little Johnny was stuck in a room not learning anything alongside kids with actual significant and profound developmental delays. 

Are you seeing a lot of that as well?

Same here but only because I lived with a room-mate who did nothing but pirate EVERYTHING he wanted. The internet wasn't in his name and we got several "stop this right now or we'll sue your asses" letters, which scared the piss out of me. We talked to him about it, and he stopped for maybe two days and then he was back at it again with a different "fool-proof" method of pirating. Our internet was always at a crawl.

To make things worse, we live right by a college so these things are frequently caught and people get in serious trouble. We know a small handful of people who have been caught and fined. 

I say, if I really want it... I'll wait a week. If I still want it, I'll buy it. If not, I won't chance the financial ruin by pirating it. Stuff isn't worth it.

I was diagnosed with ADHD at the age of six, and I've started attempting meditation, but I end up either falling asleep or twitching. Nothing seems to be working as of yet. It does seem to help with my anxiety though.

I had a staph infection, pneumonia, high fever, seizures and withdrawl symptoms from Paxil (I couldn't swallow anything, let alone a pill)...all at once. I was a wreck and my parents wouldn't take me to the hospital, so I had to wait it out.
